failure_summary.description: Three answers unnecessarily expanded personal names; another listed many valid animal sources where the expected answer was one primary source.
The missing-component instruction led to returning only “Funk” instead of the complete publisher name.
Agents answered a mentioned artwork rather than its maker, or followed an unrelated clue snippet despite direct evidence for the requested film series.
A bare pair of royal names was interpreted as asking their relationship, while the contextual answer was their shared place.

patch.reasoning: The full-name guidance can encourage unnecessary initials or given names when the clue or direct answer evidence supports a conventional shorter form. The fill-in guidance also needs a narrow exception for blanks embedded in a multiword entity name when the clue asks for that entity. The other errors already conflict with existing instructions to return one concise answer and prefer direct evidence, so repeating those rules is unlikely to help; the isolated shared-place failure also does not warrant reviving a previously rejected broad rule.

edits.target: Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component. Avoid explanations and alternatives.
edits.content: Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For an explicit fill-in or name-completion prompt, normally supply only the missing word or component; however, when a blank is embedded in a recognizable multiword entity name and the clue asks you to identify that entity, return its full canonical name. Do not repeat information already given unless it is part of the canonical answer or needed to disambiguate. For people, use the name form supported by the clue and direct evidence rather than automatically maximizing form: preserve a conventional short or surname-only answer when supported, and do not add middle initials, middle names, or extra given names unless needed to distinguish candidates. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Avoid explanations and alternatives.

edits.target: For people, give the full name rather than only a surname; include an honorific when the clue explicitly signals it, such as “knighted” requiring “Sir,” but do not add unsupported titles.
edits.content: For people, use the form supported by the clue and direct evidence, with enough detail to disambiguate; a surname or familiar first-and-last form may be canonical, so do not add middle initials or names merely to make it fuller. Include an honorific when the clue explicitly signals it, such as “knighted” requiring “Sir,” but do not add unsupported titles.
